newsitem.title: BERMUDA: CRICKET-NZ IN BOX SEAT IN 2ND TEST VS SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ IN BOX SEAT IN 2ND TEST VS SRI LANKA.

text.p: New Zealand continued to dictate terms on Monday as they closed in on victory on the fourth day of the second cricket test against Sri Lanka.
The Kiwis are well positioned to win the match, and the two-match test series 2-0, after making further inroads into the fragile Sri Lankan batting lineup in the morning session.

Sri Lanka resumed on Monday at 20 for two, requiring another 306 runs to reach their victory target of 326, but they lost another two wickets to reach the lunch break in serious bother at 81 for four.
Nightwatchman Chaminda Vaas stuck around for 41 minutes in the morning before his impatience saw him loft left-arm spinner Daniel Vettori to Dipak Patel at mid on after scoring just eight.
Seam bowler Simon Doull then struck a big blow by trapping leading Sri Lankan batsman Aravinda de Silva leg before wicket to have the tourists precariously placed at 50 for four.
De Silva had made just five and his failure continued a run of poor form. He has scored just nine runs in four innings during this series.

Opener Roshan Mahanama, who has slaved a touch under three hours for his 32, will resume after lunch with his captain Arjuna Ranatunga, whose 14 not out included successive fours to wide long-on off Vettori.
Vettori had taken two for 33 from 14 overs to be the most successful New Zealand bowler.
